title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section I of the 16-page sub-dossier 'Calculs des S_0T_G'. The aim is to compute S_0T_G when G is an 'MD' graph (the dual graph of a stable marked curve) of modular dimension 0. Every vertex is then of type (0,3), so G encodes a maximally degenerate stable curve, a 0-dimensional stratum of M̄_{g,ν}.

Step 1 (reduction to vertices). The notation G^b seems to mean G 'cut open' at its edges: a disjoint union of stars G^b_s, one per vertex s ∈ S, with A_s the half-edges at s. The page uses Â for the set of edges/arcs and \vec{Â} for the oriented edges (half-edges).
- S_0T_{G^b} is a Z^{\vec Â}-groupoid: a groupoid whose vertex groups are identified with the abelian group Z^{\vec Â}.
- S_0T_G is obtained from it by pushout of the 'internal' group along the summation map Z^{\vec Â} → Z^{Â} induced by \vec Â → Â. This is formula (1): S_0T_G = S_0T_{G^b} ∧_{Z^{\vec Â}} Z^{Â}.
- Formula (2): S_0T_{G^b} = ∏_{s∈S} S_0T_{0,\vec A_s}.
- Geometrically: at a node the circles of tangent directions of the two branches combine. The circle of directions of T_a ⊗ T_{a'} (the smoothing direction) is the quotient of T_a × T_{a'} by the antidiagonal U. On π_1 this gives Z² → Z, the sum.
- So everything reduces to S_0T_{0,I} with |I| = 3.

Step 2 (the case of P^1 with three marked points).
- Let P^1_I be the projective line marked by I. Let T_i be the circle of unit tangent rays at i; it is a U-torsor with U = {|z| = 1}.
- PU_{0,I} = ∏_i T_i is a U^I-torsor, topologically a 3-torus.
- Choose α in ω(I), one of the two orientations (cyclic orders) of I. Here is the mechanism (implicit on the page): there is a unique real circle through the three points (the fixed circle of the unique antiholomorphic involution fixing them), and α orients it. The positively oriented tangent ray at each i gives a base point, i.e. trivialisations φ_{α,i}: T_i ≅ U.
- Together these give a torsor isomorphism φ: U^I ≅ PU_{0,I}, hence a point ᾱ = φ(1).
- This yields an injection (3) ω(I) ↪ PU_{0,I}. It is equivariant for (4) {±1} → U^I, which factors as the diagonal into {±1}^I followed by the inclusion {±1} ⊂ U. Reversing the orientation reverses every tangent ray, i.e. multiplies by −1 at each point.

The next page completes this. S_0T_{0,I} is defined as the fundamental groupoid of the torus PU_{0,I} restricted to the 2-element object set ω(I): two objects, vertex groups Z^I, and morphism sets that are Z^I-torsors. Grothendieck then seeks a purely algebraic description via 0 → Z^I → R^I → U^I → 0.

Role in the larger project: this provides the 'Lego' pieces, i.e. tangential base points at maximally degenerate curves, for building the Teichmüller groupoids of Esquisse d'un programme from (0,3) pieces glued along edges.
errors: Display line: both sides are written Z^{Â} → Z^{Â}. The source should be Z^{\vec Â} (as in the preceding sentence and in (1)); this is a notational slip.
The canonicity of φ_{α,i} silently uses the unique real circle through three points of P^1. This is correct but not stated.
Minor imprecision: the identification of G^b and of Â (edges only, or also legs) is left implicit.

ideas.what: Groupoid attached to a maximally degenerate stable graph, obtained from the vertex pieces S_0T_{0,3} by pushout along the half-edge-to-edge summation Z^{half-edges} → Z^{edges}
ideas.modern_name: Lego/Teichmüller groupoid with tangential base points at maximal degeneration; gluing of (0,3) pieces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) programmatically; made explicit by Moore–Seiberg (1989), Bakalov–Kirillov (2000), Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000), Nakamura and others
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and Lego gluing qualitatively; this explicit pushout formula is not there as far as I know

ideas.what: Torus PU_G of unit tangent directions at the marked points/branches, as a U^I-torsor carrying the base points
ideas.modern_name: Fiber of the real oriented blow-up / Kato–Nakayama log Betti space over a maximally degenerate point; tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, tangential base points); Kato–Nakayama (1999); Ihara–Nakamura (1997)

ideas.what: Canonical pair of base points on P^1 minus 3 points indexed by the two cyclic orientations of I, via the real circle through the three points, swapped by diagonal −1
ideas.modern_name: Pair of 'hemispheres'/seams in a pants decomposition; the two tangential base points ±01 and their {±1}-symmetry

ideas.what: Plan to describe the fundamental groupoid of a torus-torsor purely algebraically from the extension 0→Z^I→R^I→U^I→0
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid of a torsor under a connected abelian topological group via the universal covering extension

missed.claim: Grothendieck works directly with the torus of tangent directions PU_G = ∏ T_i, with node circles obtained by pushout of half-edge circles. This is essentially the Kato–Nakayama / real-oriented-blow-up fiber over a 0-dimensional boundary stratum of M̄_{g,n}, used as the object set of the Teichmüller groupoid. It predates log-Betti formulations, and the explicit Z^{\vec A} → Z^{A} formula is a clean combinatorial statement of it.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck's Teichmüller-tower base points were conceived in a way equivalent to log-geometric tangential base points. This is mainly of historical interest; the mathematics is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, explicit unpublished formalisation of the Lego gluing at maximally degenerate points via tangent-direction tori and a pushout of Z-groupoids. The content was later rediscovered and published in equivalent forms (HLS, Bakalov–Kirillov, Nakamura, log geometry), so it is mainly historically interesting.
transcription_corrections: 'I étant un ensemble à deux [?] trois éléments' should read 'I étant un ens. à trois éléments' (a crossed-out word follows).
The display 'Z^{Â} → Z^{Â}' reflects the manuscript, but the intended source is Z^{\vec Â}.
'on est ramené à décrire [-..-] S_0T_{0,I}' probably reads 'décrire les S_0T_{0,I}'.
In the margin note, 'par le passé' is likely 'pour le passage', and 'par extension' is likely 'profinis'; this reading is uncertain.
